title: The recognition and estimation of cyclic trends.
data_setting: Event counts by time of year
key_idea: Test annual cyclic pattern using harmonic representation
assumptions: Single dominant sinusoid; event dates meaningful
limitations: Best for counts/events rather than continuous phenotypes

citation: Walter SD, Elwood JM. Br J Prev Soc Med. 1975.
title: A test for seasonality of events with a variable population at risk.
journal_or_book: British Journal of Preventive and Social Medicine
data_setting: Event counts with varying population at risk
key_idea: Harmonic test adjusted for unequal exposure and month length
limitations: Still event-focused, not ideal for covariate-rich continuous outcomes
notes: Useful if analyzing event counts from image-derived thresholds

title: Methods for current statistical analysis of excess pneumonia-influenza deaths.
key_idea: Model seasonal baseline with sine/cosine terms
assumptions: Smooth trend plus recurring seasonal baseline
limitations: Designed for regular aggregated series
notes: Important historical reference for harmonic terms

citation: Stolwijk AM, Straatman H, Zielhuis GA. J Epidemiol Community Health. 1999.
title: Studying seasonality by using sine and cosine functions in regression analysis.
journal_or_book: Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health
key_idea: Represent seasonality with sine and cosine covariates
assumptions: Seasonality approximately sinusoidal unless higher harmonics added
strengths: Highly transferable, easy covariate adjustment, works with irregular timing
limitations: Misses complex seasonal shapes if only one harmonic used
notes: One of the most directly relevant references

citation: Nelson W, Tong YL, Lee JK, Halberg F. Chronobiologia. 1979.
title: Methods for cosinor-rhythmometry.
key_idea: Estimate mesor, amplitude, phase for known period
limitations: Parametric and period-dependent

citation: Lentz MJ. West J Nurs Res. 1990.
title: Time-series analysis, cosinor analysis: a special case.
key_idea: Introductory explanation of cosinor as regression/time-series special case
limitations: Not a deep technical source

citation: Cornelissen G. Theor Biol Med Model. 2014.
title: Cosinor-based rhythmometry.
key_idea: Single and extended cosinor models for rhythmic data
strengths: Best biomedical review; discusses non-equidistant data
limitations: Still largely parametric

title: Statistical Analysis of Circular Data.
key_idea: Treat season as circular variable and analyze phase concentration/differences
limitations: Less natural for multivariable continuous-outcome regression
notes: Useful for timing of peak effect

title: Directional Statistics.
key_idea: General theory for inference on circular or directional variables
limitations: Abstract and not application-specific

title: Least-squares frequency analysis of unequally spaced data.
key_idea: Spectral analysis without regular spacing
limitations: Limited confounder adjustment in basic form

title: Studies in astronomical time series analysis. II. Statistical aspects of spectral analysis of unevenly spaced data.
key_idea: Statistical framework for unevenly sampled spectral analysis
limitations: Mostly exploratory unless extended

title: Understanding the Lomb-Scargle Periodogram.
key_idea: Practical review of Lomb-Scargle variants and interpretation
limitations: Still not the main covariate-adjusted inferential tool

title: Spectral Analysis and Time Series.
key_idea: Frequency-domain decomposition of variation
limitations: Not the easiest primary tool for MRI phenotype inference

citation: Torrence C, Compo GP. Bull Amer Meteor Soc. 1998.
title: A practical guide to wavelet analysis.
journal_or_book: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
data_setting: Signals whose periodicity may vary over time
key_idea: Time-frequency decomposition for nonstationary periodic signals
strengths: Useful if seasonal amplitude changes across years
limitations: More complex and less interpretable as primary clinical test

citation: Cleveland RB, Cleveland WS, McRae JE, Terpenning I. J Off Stat. 1990.
title: STL: A Seasonal-Trend Decomposition Procedure Based on Loess.
key_idea: Separate trend, seasonal, remainder components with robust loess
strengths: Flexible seasonal shape, strong exploratory tool
limitations: Needs regular spacing or preprocessing

citation: Hyndman RJ, Athanasopoulos G. Forecasting: Principles and Practice.
title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice.
key_idea: Practical seasonal modeling using Fourier terms and state-space forecasting
limitations: Inference for subject-level phenotypes is not the main focus

citation: De Livera AM, Hyndman RJ, Snyder RD. JASA. 2011.
title: Forecasting time series with complex seasonal patterns using exponential smoothing.
journal_or_book: Journal of the American Statistical Association
key_idea: Model multiple/complex seasonal cycles
limitations: Forecasting-oriented and prefers regular spacing
notes: Lower priority for your main analysis

title: Generalized Additive Models: An Introduction with R.
key_idea: Use cyclic smooths of day-of-year with covariate adjustment
strengths: Excellent for nonlinear seasonality, covariates, and interactions
limitations: Needs careful smoothing/inference choices

title: Generalized Additive Models.
key_idea: Flexible additive structure including smooth seasonal effects
limitations: Older reference, less implementation detail than Wood

title: Forecasting, Structural Time Series Models and the Kalman Filter.
data_setting: Series with latent trend and seasonality
key_idea: Model seasonal pattern as latent state
strengths: Elegant handling of missingness and evolving seasonal structure
limitations: More complex and less transparent than harmonic regression

title: Time Series Analysis by State Space Methods.
data_setting: Observed data with latent temporal states
key_idea: Kalman filter / smoother for seasonal components and irregular observation structures
limitations: Technically heavy

citation: Box GEP, Jenkins GM, Reinsel GC, Ljung GM.
title: Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control.
key_idea: Model autocorrelation and seasonality through differencing and ARIMA terms
assumptions: Regular spacing and stationarity after transforms
limitations: Poor fit to irregular patient-level visit dates
notes: Useful mostly for aggregated monthly summaries

title: The Econometric Analysis of Seasonal Time Series.
key_idea: Formal theory for seasonal structure, tests, and transformations
strengths: Strong theory on seasonal processes and testing
limitations: Much of the machinery targets macroeconomic series

citation: Edwards JH; Walter SD & Elwood JM; Stolwijk AM et al. Various.
title: Classical event-seasonality tests.
key_idea: Use circular/harmonic tests on dates of events
limitations: Not suitable as sole analysis for MRI phenotypes
